title: The Environments surface: UP DEGRADED DOWN with a latency sparkline, and backups showing restore-proof state
description:
SPIDR grandchild A of task-f008f29a38d54ae7a10e97cad1c4443d (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05), split because the parent carried four UI surfaces plus a Playwright journey, a live drive and docs - measured at thirteen-plus files against a ten-file ceiling. This row owns the parent's DoD 1 and 5. It carries the parent's dependsOn unchanged.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the Deployments card (UP / DEGRADED / DOWN, last probe time, latency sparkline over the last hour) and the backups list showing RESTORE-PROOF state, plus the 'Environments' section on the Health screen that hosts them.

PUT IT IN ITS OWN MODULE. Measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx is 236 LINES against a 250 ceiling - it grew from 228 while the parent was being planned. A new section written inline pushes it over. ops-screens.tsx should gain little more than the wiring.

SHOW RESTORE-PROOF STATE, NOT BACKUP EXISTENCE. Child 2 (task-95e68a8d) records a restore-to-temp sha256 per backup precisely so 'a backup exists' and 'a backup has been proven restorable' are different facts. A list that renders only existence hides the distinction that row exists to establish, and it is the distinction an operator relies on at the worst possible moment. Render three states - proven / failed / not yet checked - and never collapse 'not yet checked' into 'proven'.

READ WHAT THE DAEMON STATES. The probe ring and the derived UP/DEGRADED/DOWN belong to child 1's grandchild task-cc05c47362dc41b0b2b416a70ad45b42; this row RENDERS them and derives nothing of its own. If the frame does not carry a fact you need, that is a comment on that row and a report_blocked here - not a client-side derivation, which would put a second UP/DOWN opinion in the browser.

CONCURRENCY: apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx is being edited by task-84cd2e55 ('The operator deploys an environment from the goal and sees where...'), which is WORKING and is deployment UI adjacent to this. Rebase, never delete a peer's entry, and check the testid namespace you choose is free before using it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the Needs-you incident card, Roll back / Dismiss (grandchild B); the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs (grandchild C).

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.
definitionOfDone: The Deployments card renders UP / DEGRADED / DOWN with the last probe time and a latency sparkline over the last hour, driven by a REAL daemon frame rather than a hand-built fixture object - assert against the shape the daemon actually serves, so a frame change breaks this test rather than production.

The state shown is the one the DAEMON derived: assert the card renders what the frame says and does NOT recompute UP/DEGRADED/DOWN in the browser. A client-side derivation is a second opinion that will eventually disagree with the daemon about the same ring.

The backups list renders each backup's RESTORE-PROOF state as three distinct values - proven / failed / not yet checked - asserted separately. Assert specifically that 'not yet checked' is NOT rendered as proven: collapsing them hides the exact distinction the restore check exists to establish.

The Health screen gains an 'Environments' section in its own module, and apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx stays under the 250-line ceiling - quote its line count before and after in the completion record. It was 236 at filing.

Any new read is decoded EXACT-KEY with a dev-proxy-paths pin, matching how every other live read client in this app works; and the sources are ASCII-only with apostrophe-free JSX text (the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on an apostrophe in JSX).
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: RENDER WHAT THE DAEMON STATES, DERIVE NOTHING. UP/DEGRADED/DOWN is computed from the probe ring by the daemon; a browser-side recomputation is a second source of truth about one history.
SHOW RESTORE-PROOF STATE IN THREE VALUES. 'Not yet checked' must never render as proven - that collapse is the failure this surface exists to prevent.
OWN MODULE, NOT INLINE. ops-screens.tsx was 236 lines against a 250 ceiling at filing and is being edited concurrently by task-84cd2e55; it should gain only wiring.
REBASE, DO NOT DELETE A PEER'S ENTRY. Three rows are editing this area concurrently; check your testid namespace is free before claiming it.
ASCII-ONLY SOURCES, APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT, EXACT-KEY decoders, dev-proxy-paths pin for any new read.
NO INCIDENT CARD, NO ROLLBACK CONTROL, NO PLAYWRIGHT, NO LIVE DRIVE, NO DOCS - grandchildren B and C.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE THE FRAME BEFORE NAMING A SINGLE FIELD. This row RENDERS facts two other rows produce, and neither had landed at plan time (2026-09-05), so this plan deliberately names no field of theirs:
  - the probe ring and the derived UP/DEGRADED/DOWN come from task-cc05c47362dc41b0b2b416a70ad45b42 (under task-6ec875f4, in this row's dependsOn)
  - the per-backup restore-proof state comes from task-95e68a8dd2464e7b8ad4b1f8c4d2b2e4 (also in dependsOn)
Your dependsOn gates the WORKING claim until both land, so the real shapes exist when you run. Read each row's completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings and RECORD the exact field names, then plan your decoder against those. If either frame is absent, `moe.report_blocked` with the missing row id rather than inventing a shape — an invented field decodes to undefined and renders as a plausible blank.

Re-measure the three moving local facts and print them:
  (a) `wc -l apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx` — it was 236 against a 250 ceiling at filing, up from 228 a few hours earlier. If it is already at or over 250, say so: your section still goes in its own module, but the wiring line you add needs somewhere to go and that is a stop-and-report rather than a squeeze.
  (b) `grep -rn 'cr\.health\.' apps/control-room/src --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts | head` — the testid namespace convention is `cr.<screen>.<thing>` (see ops-screens.tsx:107-196). Confirm the ids you intend to claim are FREE before using them; task-84cd2e55 is WORKING on this same file and may have taken some.
  (c) `git log --oneline -5 -- apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx` — see what the peer has landed so you rebase onto it rather than over it.

THE READ CLIENT — EXACT-KEY AT EVERY LEVEL, plus the proxy pin. Write the decoder and its RED tests before any rendering.

Copy the discipline in `apps/control-room/src/live/live-ops.ts`, whose header (:4) states it: "exact-key snapshots at every level (the discipline of live-planning-run.ts)". The helper is `exactDataRecord(value, […keys])` and every call passes a SORTED key list — see :119, :127, :205, :226 for nested examples. Exact-key means a frame carrying an unexpected key is REFUSED, not silently ignored: that is the property that makes a daemon-side shape change break this client's tests instead of production, and it is why the key list must match the frame exactly rather than listing only what you read.

PIN THE ROUTE. `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` exports a frozen `DEV_PROXY_PATHS` array of every project-daemon route the v2 browser may proxy in development. A new read route MUST be added there or it works in production and silently fails in the dev proxy — a failure that looks like an empty surface rather than an error.

RED ARMS:
  1. A well-formed frame decodes, every field asserted by value.
  2. A frame with an EXTRA key is refused — assert the refusal, not just that decoding did not return the extra key.
  3. A frame MISSING a key is refused.
  4. The refusal path renders the existing `Refusal` component rather than a blank section, matching how PolicyScreen (:110) and HealthScreen (:208) already handle an unreadable outcome — an operator seeing an empty Environments section cannot tell "nothing deployed" from "the read failed".
  5. The loading state renders too (the screens use a `cr2-slot-kicker` "Reading the …" line, :107 and :208). A surface that renders nothing while loading reads as an empty environment list.

THE ENVIRONMENTS SECTION — its own module under apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/, NOT inline in ops-screens.tsx (rail 3).

Render UP / DEGRADED / DOWN and the last probe time FROM THE FRAME. DERIVE NOTHING (rail 1, DoD 2). The daemon computes the state from the probe ring; a browser-side recomputation is a second opinion about one history, and when the two disagree the operator sees the browser's. Concretely: do not re-derive the state from the latency values you already have for the sparkline just because they are in hand. Add an arm that feeds a frame whose stated status DISAGREES with what a naive client-side rule would compute, and assert the rendered state follows the FRAME — that is the only arm that actually catches a hidden derivation, since a consistent fixture passes either way.

Follow the house shape from ops-screens.tsx: a `<section className="cr2-ops" data-testid="cr.<name>.root">` with `cr2-ops-card` children, and `data-<attr>` hooks for state the way :128 uses `data-installed`. Prefer a `data-status` attribute carrying the state verbatim over asserting on visible words — it survives copy changes, and copy on this surface is likely to be revised.

ASCII-ONLY SOURCES AND APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT (rail 5). This is not style: an apostrophe in JSX text reds the scheduler package-boundary scan, which fails in a lane far from this file and reads as unrelated. Write "the operator cannot" rather than a contraction, and keep every character ASCII.

EMPTY AND UNPROBEABLE ARE DIFFERENT STATES, and both are real on day one: a project with no deployed environment renders an empty-state line (see the `cr.policy.empty` shape at :162), and an environment that exists but cannot be probed renders its refusal rather than a blank or a green. Assert both — an unprobeable environment reading as healthy is the worst output this surface can produce.

THE SPARKLINE AND THE BACKUPS LIST.

SPARKLINE, last hour of latency. There is NO chart precedent in this app — `grep -rln 'sparkline|polyline' apps/control-room/src/v2 --include=*.tsx` finds only shell files matching on unrelated svg. So draw it as INLINE SVG and add NO charting dependency: a library for one sparkline is a bundle and a supply-chain edge this surface does not need.

Make it assertable and safe on the degenerate inputs it will actually meet:
  - ZERO points (a brand-new environment): render the empty state, never an SVG with NaN coordinates. Assert it.
  - ONE point: no division-by-zero when scaling across a range of width zero. Assert it — this is the classic sparkline crash and a new environment hits it immediately.
  - All-identical latencies: same zero-range hazard on the Y axis.
  - Assert the plotted point COUNT matches the window, so a sparkline silently drawing the whole ring instead of the last hour is caught.
Give the SVG an accessible name and keep the numbers reachable as text or an attribute — a chart whose values exist only as path geometry cannot be asserted, and cannot be read by anyone using a screen reader.

BACKUPS LIST — THREE DISTINCT VALUES (rail 2, DoD 3): proven / failed / not yet checked. Assert each separately, and assert specifically that NOT-YET-CHECKED DOES NOT RENDER AS PROVEN. That collapse is the whole failure this surface exists to prevent: child 2 records a restore-to-temp sha256 per backup precisely so "a backup exists" and "a backup has been proven restorable" are different facts, and an operator leans on that difference at the worst possible moment. Carry the state in a `data-` attribute so the arm does not depend on wording, and make the three visually distinguishable rather than distinguished only by colour.

WIRE IT INTO THE HEALTH SCREEN, AND KEEP THE FILE UNDER ITS CEILING.

`HealthScreen` is at apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx:201. Add the Environments section as a CHILD COMPONENT CALL — ops-screens.tsx should gain the import and the element, and little else (rail 3). It was 236 lines against a 250 ceiling at filing and had grown 8 lines in the hours before; quote `wc -l` before and after in the completion record (DoD 4).

REBASE, DO NOT OVERWRITE (rail 4). task-84cd2e55 is WORKING in this exact file and is deployment UI adjacent to yours. If your rebase drops one of its entries the loss is silent — its tests live in its own files and will not red here. After rebasing, `git diff` the file and confirm every hunk is YOURS; anything you do not recognise is the peer's and stays.

If ops-screens.tsx is at or over 250 by the time you land, do NOT shave unrelated lines to make room and do NOT inline your section to avoid the import. Report it: the file needs a split, that split is not this row's scope, and squeezing it is how the next row inherits an unreviewable file.

GATES AND DRILLS.

GATES, each STANDALONE and FOREGROUND — no pipe, no `;` chain, no `&&` (a piped run reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`
  2. `pnpm typecheck`
READ THE OUTPUT, NOT THE EXIT CODE: a missed `--filter` exits 0, and "No test files found" / "0 passed" are also exit 0. The discriminator is `Test Files N passed` with N nonzero — quote it for both. A bare `pnpm test` covers NO `apps/**` file, so it is not evidence for anything in this row. Name `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` as the complete_task verification command.

DRILL 1, THE HIDDEN DERIVATION. Change the module to compute UP/DEGRADED/DOWN from the latency values instead of reading the frame's stated status. The disagreeing-frame arm from step 3 MUST go red. If it stays green, that arm is using a fixture whose stated status happens to agree with the naive rule — rewrite the fixture so the two genuinely differ, because as written it proves nothing.
DRILL 2, THE COLLAPSE. Render "not yet checked" the same as "proven". The backups arm must go red. If it only reds on a count, it is asserting how many rows exist rather than what each says.
DRILL 3, THE DECODER. Add an unexpected key to the frame fixture. The exact-key arm must go red — that is the property that makes a daemon shape change break this client instead of production.

RESTORE PROOF, global rail 13. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths BEFORE drilling. ops-screens.tsx, live-ops.ts and dev-proxy-paths.ts are TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is valid proof, run in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Your NEW module and its test are UNTRACKED and `git diff` is BLIND to them — back each up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) before mutating and prove the restore by SHA256 equality against that backup.

COMPLETION RECORD states: the frame field names you decoded and which row produced each; ops-screens.tsx line count before and after against its 250 ceiling; the testids you claimed and that you confirmed them free; that the sparkline is inline SVG with no dependency added, plus its zero-point and single-point behaviour; and the three drill outcomes with restore proofs.

GAP 1, DoD 1's SPARKLINE - NO LATENCY SERIES IS SERVED.
`/deployments/health/read` projects ONE point: `lastProbeOf` (apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts:175-181) returns `probes.at(-1)`, and `DeploymentsHealthView.lastProbe` (:66-68) is `{at, latencyMs, status} | null`. The FULL ring is already at the port as `DeploymentsHealthSource.probes: readonly HealthProbe[]` (:86) and is deliberately narrowed out at the view. One point is not an hour of latency; rendering it as a sparkline would be a narrowed DoD, and a component with no producer is dead code.
I did NOT widen the view myself: that changes a RETURNED SHAPE whose asserting consumers are outside this row's owned-path roster - deployments-health-read.test.ts (20 exact-shape arms) and daemon-entry-deployments-health.test.ts (6 arms). The global roster rail says a worker who finds an unnamed consumer mid-step stops and reports. Filed as task-a98b01a44ffd46cba9d9648fcb7001cb (order 121.85, dependsOn cc05c473 + 509c6c16). It is a view widening plus consumers, not new plumbing.

GAP 2, DoD 3's BACKUPS LIST - NOTHING IS SERVED AT ALL.
apps/daemon/src/backups/scheduled-backup.ts computes the fact (`status: "VERIFIED" | "FAILED"` :21, `sha256` :23, `proof` :24) and `grep -rn "scheduled-backup" apps/daemon/src` OUTSIDE its own directory returns ZERO importers. No port, no route, no composition edge; the served roster (http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:78-110) has no backups path. There is nothing to decode. Separately the served type is only TWO-valued: "written but restore-check not yet run" cannot be expressed, and that third value is the whole point of DoD 3. Filed as task-1f994315fd164a789424349cb7bba4ca (order 122.05, dependsOn 95e68a8d).
CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: the plan's DRILL 2 (render not-yet-checked as proven, watch the arm red) was NOT RUN and I am not reporting it as passed. A drill against a surface that does not exist would be a fabricated proof.

A THIRD GAP I SOLVED RATHER THAN BLOCKED ON. No served route enumerates DEPLOYED environments project-wide: `/deployments/read` is goal-scoped and the Health screen holds no goal (LiveActivity there is passed goalRef={null}); `/environments/read` takes one environment name. A fixed-roster fan-out over ENVIRONMENT_NAMES (apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-contracts.ts:29 = preview/production/verify) would be WRONG, not merely wasteful: a never-deployed environment returns an empty probe ring, which the daemon states as DEGRADED, so a fresh project would show three degraded environments that do not exist and "nothing deployed" would stop being distinguishable from "deployed and unwell". LiveEnvironments assembles the set from served reads only: goal catalog -> /deployments/read per goal (capped at MAX_GOALS 12) -> union of outcome DEPLOYED -> one health read each. Asserted by recording the calls: the REFUSED environment is never asked for health, and a project with nothing deployed triggers ZERO health reads.

DELIVERED, GREEN, ON DISK - 10 paths declared via moe.declare_files:
NEW apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts (216 ln) + .test.ts (13 arms); NEW apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx (178 ln) + .test.tsx (9 arms); NEW apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/live-environments.tsx (132 ln) + .test.tsx (9 arms); MOD dev-proxy-paths.ts (pin), live-document-proxy.test.ts (whole-array roster pin), http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts (BOTH censuses retired - I am the first consumer, per task-509c6c16's handoff), live-ops.tsx (+2 lines).

DoD 4 DETAIL: ops-screens.tsx is 238 BEFORE and 238 AFTER against its 250 ceiling (236 at filing), and UNTOUCHED - `git status --porcelain` on it is empty. I wired into LiveHealth (live-ops.tsx:137) rather than into HealthScreen because ops-screens.tsx:12-17 documents HealthScreen as pure ("No fetch, no clock beyond the nowMs handed in") and every other fetching section on Health - LiveRepositoryRecovery, LiveSessions, LiveActivity - is already composed there. This satisfies rail 3 more strictly than the plan asked: ops-screens.tsx gains ZERO lines rather than two.

FRAME FIELDS DECODED AND THEIR PRODUCERS: environment, incident, lastError, lastProbe, ok, probeRefusal, rollbackSha, state - all from /deployments/health/read (route by task-509c6c16; probe ring and the derived `state` by task-cc05c473). Deployment enumeration from /deployments/read (task-84cd2e55's client, CONSUMED not edited). Nothing from task-95e68a8d is decoded, because it serves nothing over HTTP.

TWO DECODER DEFECTS THE MEASUREMENT CAUGHT, both fixed: (1) the probe-store refusal `{code, layer, ok:false}` is NOT matched by the shared effectRefusal helper (live-effect-read.ts:45 stops at {code,layer} and {outcome,code,layer}, and effectRecord is strict on key COUNT), so PROBE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE would have decoded as a generic invalid response with its cause erased; (2) a NULL member and an UNREADABLE member both return null from a nested decoder, so each is re-checked against the RAW member - a malformed lastProbe now refuses the whole frame instead of reading as "no probe yet".

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT AND I FIXED IT BEFORE BLOCKING. The first cut read catalog.goals and ignored catalog.outcome, and swallowed a thrown read with `.catch(() => undefined)`. A catalog that REFUSED / was UNDELIVERED / was UNREADABLE has `goals: []`, so the section would have rendered "No environment deployed." about a project it could not read - this row's risk 3 exactly, and the one sentence this surface must never say without knowing it. FIX: a section-level `refusal` prop that OUTRANKS loading, empty and list; four stable codes at layer CONTROL_ROOM_ENVIRONMENTS - ENVIRONMENTS_CATALOG_{REFUSED,UNDELIVERED,UNREADABLE} and ENVIRONMENTS_READ_FAILED. Four new arms assert the SPECIFIC code and assert `cr.environments.empty` and `cr.environments.list` are ABSENT.

Its UNCONSUMED census is a reachability walk of the SHIPPED production tree, so this green is the proof the wiring is a real call site and not a type-only referent.

DRILLS. Restore proof FIRST: `git status --porcelain` showed both drill targets UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind and inadmissible; each was backed up to %TEMP%/drill-worker-b1872f24/ and the restore proven by SHA256 equality in a SEPARATE call.
 - DRILL 1 (derivation): replaced `data-status={view.state}` with a client rule over lastProbe. RED, 4 arms. The one that matters: "follows the FRAME when the stated status disagrees with the probe material" -> `expected 'DOWN' to be 'UP'`, fired in the right direction, proving the fixture genuinely disagrees rather than being the consistent kind that passes either way. Restored, sha256 4752c8be...98d4, `grep -c "DRILL 1 MUTANT"` = 0.

Exact-key REFUSES an unexpected key rather than ignoring it, which is what makes a daemon-side shape change break this client's tests instead of production. The key list must mirror the frame exactly, not just the fields the UI reads.

THE PROXY PIN IS A REAL FAILURE MODE, not paperwork: `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` exports a frozen `DEV_PROXY_PATHS` roster of every project-daemon route the v2 browser may proxy in development. A new route omitted from it works in production and fails in the dev proxy — and the symptom is an empty surface, not an error.

planningNotes.risks:
1. A HIDDEN CLIENT-SIDE DERIVATION. The latency values are in hand for the sparkline, so recomputing the state from them is the natural shortcut — and it puts a second opinion about one probe ring in the browser, which is the one the operator sees when the two disagree. Only a disagreeing-frame fixture catches it; drill 1 proves the fixture is the disagreeing kind.

2. 'NOT YET CHECKED' RENDERING AS PROVEN. It fails safe-LOOKING: the operator believes a backup is restorable when nobody has tried. This is the precise distinction child 2's restore check exists to establish, so collapsing it here silently discards that row's whole value.

3. AN UNPROBEABLE OR UNREADABLE ENVIRONMENT RENDERING AS BLANK OR GREEN. An empty section cannot be told from "nothing deployed", and a green one is actively misleading. Loading, empty, refusal and unprobeable are four distinct states and the plan requires each rendered and asserted.

4. THE SPARKLINE'S DEGENERATE INPUTS. Zero points is a brand-new environment — the common case on day one — and one point or all-identical latencies divide by a zero range. NaN coordinates render as an invisible or broken path rather than an error.

5. A MISSING DEV_PROXY_PATHS ENTRY. Works in production, fails in the dev proxy, and the symptom is an empty surface rather than an error — so it survives a casual manual check.

6. A SILENT REBASE LOSS. task-84cd2e55 is live in ops-screens.tsx; dropping one of its hunks reds nothing here because its tests are elsewhere. The plan requires diffing the file after rebase and confirming every hunk is this row's.

7. THE 250-LINE CEILING moving under the row — the file gained 8 lines in the hours before planning.

8. AN APOSTROPHE IN JSX TEXT reds the scheduler package-boundary scan in a distant lane, where it reads as an unrelated failure.
